reason: The text explicitly establishes and emphasizes strict hierarchies throughout. It depicts Pharaoh as supreme ruler (וַיֻּגַּד לְמֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם), his servants as subordinate (וַעֲבָדָיו), Moses as the authoritative leader the Israelites turn to for guidance (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה), and God as the ultimate authority above all (יְהוָה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם). Authority structures are foundational to the narrative's functioning—Pharaoh commands, Moses leads, God directs. Hierarchy is neither unimportant nor discouraged; it is integral to the text's organization and meaning.
